title: Remove native custom emoji committed by a cancelled upload request
classification: Confirmed lifecycle gap: the native upload routes waited for image-worker completion on cancellation, but did not undo a successful row/file commit whose response was cancelled.

change.routes: Both JSON and legacy native upload handlers use a shared cancellable adapter. If cancellation arrives during worker execution, the adapter waits for completion, then removes the exact row by primary key and expected opaque filename before propagating cancellation.
change.cleanup: The upload file is removed only after the matching database row is committed as deleted; mismatched IDs or filenames are preserved. Cleanup errors are logged without exposing paths or masking request cancellation.

verification.database_result: passed: 11 tests on Python 3.14.10 and PostgreSQL 17.6
verification.database: Fresh oneirodexemoji_cancel_test database upgraded from Alembic baseline through head; dropped after verification. TEST_DATABASE_URL was process-scoped; root .env unchanged.
verification.coverage: The native JSON upload route delegates to the cancellable adapter. Direct task cancellation waits for worker completion and invokes exact-row cleanup; the database helper preserves a row/file on mismatched filename and removes the matching row/file. A synthetic file-unlink failure creates a retry job that the generic post-commit worker successfully processes. Existing generic AnyIO/direct task cancellation and upload-work-slot tests pass.

limits: The cancellation regression exercises the shared native upload adapter, not a real browser disconnect against the HTTP route.

Emoji-specific health responsiveness and real client-disconnect testing remain open; health was directly exercised through the game-art adapter and generic cleanup restart behavior was separately verified in R1978.
